finding.claim: Mail::Message.from_yaml lets attacker-supplied YAML overwrite @delivery_method with a Mail::Sendmail object whose settings[:location] is /bin/sh, giving command execution on deliver!. Requires attacker control of the full YAML document and an app that delivers the result.
finding.sink: message.rb:1866 instance_variable_set(@delivery_method) -> message.rb:269 delivery_method.deliver! -> sendmail.rb:80 IO.popen(command)

trace.note: permitted_classes includes Mail::Sendmail (line 13) and Symbol; safe_load does not restrict ivars
any key starting with '@' is accepted

finding.guards_checked: safe_load class allowlist (permitted Mail::Sendmail, Mail::SMTP, Mail::FileDelivery); no ivar allowlist in from_yaml; no check on delivery_method type. Also delivery_handler Object.const_get at message.rb:1858 is unrestricted.

finding.claim: Header#[]= rejects only colons in field names, so CR/LF in a header name is emitted raw, allowing injection of arbitrary headers and body content when the app passes attacker-controlled hash keys.
finding.source: Hash keys passed to Mail.new(hash), Message#headers(hash) (message.rb:455-458), init_with_hash (message.rb:2107), or Message#[]= (message.rb:1331)
finding.sink: optional_field.rb:12 / unstructured_field.rb:96 emit "#{name}: ..." unescaped into the encoded message

trace.note: only COLON is rejected in name
Field constructor checks only for colon
wrap_lines emits raw name with CRLF

finding.guards_checked: Header colon check (header.rb:149); Field colon check (field.rb:197); CRLF encoding applies only to values (unstructured_field.rb:179-183), not names; SmtpEnvelope CR/LF check (smtp_envelope.rb:50) covers recipients/sender only, not header text. SMTP dot-stuffing prevents early DATA termination.

finding.claim: POP3 retrieval hard-codes OpenSSL::SSL::VERIFY_NONE when enable_ssl is set, so a network MITM can read or alter POP3 credentials and mail.
finding.source: Network position between the app and the POP3 server

trace.note: pop3.start sends user_name/password over the unverified TLS session

finding.guards_checked: No openssl_verify_mode or CA option exists for POP3 (pop3.rb:39-45). Contrast smtp.rb:187-198, where verification defaults on.

finding.claim: IMAPS retrieval passes verify=false positionally to Net::IMAP.new, disabling certificate verification, so a network MITM can read or alter IMAP credentials and mail.
finding.source: Network position between the app and the IMAP server
finding.sink: imap.rb:170 Net::IMAP.new(address, port, enable_ssl, nil, false)

trace.note: imap.login sends credentials over the unverified connection

finding.guards_checked: No option exposes verification; legacy positional net-imap signature assumed (not checked against the installed version). enable_starttls path is a separate branch (imap.rb:172).

finding.claim: ENCODED_VALUE regex (lazy .*? with no length cap) may be super-linear on long RFC 2047 header values lacking a '?=' terminator, a possible CPU DoS when decoding untrusted headers. Unverified; low confidence.
finding.source: Untrusted inbound header value read through #decoded or #subject

trace.note: line.gsub!(ENCODED_VALUE) scans each =?..?= start with lazy .*?

finding.guards_checked: No length limit found in the decode path. Ruby 3.2+ regex memoization may mitigate; not measured (Bash unavailable).
